title: Chapter 101: Hensheng: To Hate Life 4
content:
Chapter 101

Jin Ling shot straight up. "Jiujiu!"

Jiang Cheng cut a freezing glare across the room. "Oh, now you know how to call me? You weren't yelling for me when you ran off earlier!"

With that, his gaze flicked, half-deliberate and half-accidental, toward Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji. Before their eyes could even meet, Su She pushed himself up with the help of his sword, Nanping, and lunged for Jiang Cheng. Before Jiang Cheng could even raise a hand, a burst of furious barking echoed from outside, and Fairy came barreling through the doors like a flying torpedo, diving straight at Su She's throat.

The moment that bark hit Wei Wuxian's ears, every hair on his body stood on end. His soul practically took flight as he dove headfirst into Lan Wangji’s chest, terrified out of his wits: "Lan Zhan!"

Lan Wangji’s arm was already around his waist, holding him tight. "Mn! I'm here."

Even without looking at the pair, the mere sound of that exchange sent a visible twitch rippling across Jiang Cheng's face. If he’d had even the slightest inclination to look in their direction before, his neck was now locked dead-straight.

Right then, a squad of monks and cultivators charged out from the back hall, blades drawn. Jiang Cheng sneered. Snapping his right wrist, he whipped Zidian around the temple in a dazzling arc of violet lightning. Anyone caught in its blistering wake was hurled through the air, yet through it all, the oiled-paper umbrella in his left hand never wavered so much as an inch.

Only when the room was littered with bodies writhing and convulsing from the electric shock did Jiang Cheng finally fold his umbrella. Across the floor, Su She was locked in a bitter struggle with the black spiritual hound, swearing at the top of his lungs, while Jin Ling cheered from the sidelines: "Fairy, watch out! Fairy, bite him! Go for his hands!"

Lan Xichen called out a sharp warning: "Jiang-zongzhu, watch out for the guqin chords!"

The warning had barely cleared his lips when a few clear, sharp zither notes chimed from the back of the temple. But Jiang Cheng had already learned his lesson the hard way on the Burial Mounds and wasn't about to be caught flat-footed twice. The instant that chord twanged, he kicked a fallen sword off the floor with the toe of his boot, tossed his umbrella aside to catch it with his left hand, and whipped Sandu out of its sheath with his right.

Crossing the twin blades in an iron grip, he dragged them against each other.

Screeech!

Metal ground against metal, unleashing a deafening, ear-splitting shriek that completely smothered Jin Guangyao’s melody.

A ridiculously effective counter—with only one tiny problem. The noise was pure, unadulterated torture.

It felt like someone was driving rusty nails straight through their eardrums. For cultivators of the Gusu Lan Sect, who practically held refined pitch as sacred, the racket was intolerable; both Lan Xichen and Lan Wangji winced in unison. But Lan Wangji had his hands full dutifully playing human shield for Wei Wuxian, leaving him unable to cover his own ears.

Seeing this, Wei Wuxian—shivering like a leaf every time Fairy barked—reached up with both hands and clamped them tightly over Lan Wangji’s ears for him.

Stone-faced, Jiang Cheng pressed forward toward the back hall, maintaining that horrific, screeching racket the entire way. But before he could breach the inner sanctuary, Jin Guangyao strolled out of his own accord, clapping hands over his ears.

"Jiang-zongzhu," Jin Guangyao grimaced, "I yield. That move of yours is lethal."

Jiang Cheng answered with a violent crack of Zidian. Jin Guangyao danced back to dodge it. "Jiang-zongzhu! How did you even track us here?"

Jiang Cheng didn't waste his breath on pleasantries. Outmatched in raw spiritual power, Jin Guangyao didn't dare take him head-on; he ducked and weaved through the hall, sending his disciples in waves to pin Jiang Cheng down while he kept up a breezy, casual chatter: "Did A-Ling run off, and you chased him all the way here? I bet Fairy led the way, too. Ah, to think I’m the one who gifted him that hound, and it won't even cut me a shred of slack."

Tucked securely in Lan Wangji's arms, the barking didn't sound quite as terrifying anymore, and Wei Wuxian’s brain finally started ticking again. Watching Jin Guangyao dodge strikes while his eyes darted and that fake little smile never left his face, Wei Wuxian was struck by an eerie sense of familiarity.

"He's cut from the exact same cloth as Xue Yang," Wei Wuxian muttered under his breath.

Lan Wangji didn't respond. Wei Wuxian blinked, glancing up—only to realize his hands were still glued over Lan Wangji's ears. The man hadn't heard a single syllable. Flushing, Wei Wuxian yanked his hands away.

Right then, Jin Guangyao abruptly pivoted, his tone dripping with mock amusement: "Jiang-zongzhu, what's with you? You've been dodging and averting your eyes this whole time, terrified to look over there. Is there something scary in the corner?"

"You're the Chief Cultivator," Jiang Cheng spat. "If you want to throw down, throw down! What's with all the damn running commentary?!"

"Still looking away?" Jin Guangyao chuckled. "There's nothing over there—just your shixiong. Tell me, did you really come all this way just chasing after A-Ling?"

"Who the hell else would I be looking for?!" Jiang Cheng barked.

"Do not answer him!" Lan Xichen shouted.

Jin Guangyao was a master of psychological warfare; the second Jiang Cheng took the bait, his focus would fracture and his temper would run the show.

Jin Guangyao sighed, turning his head. "Well now, Wei-xiansheng, you see that? Your shidi didn't come for you, and he can't even stand to look at you."

Wei Wuxian gave a dry laugh. "That's a weird point to make. It's not like Jiang-zongzhu's attitude toward me is breaking news. Do you really think I need you to point that out?"

Jiang Cheng's jaw clenched so hard the muscles jumped, veins bulging along the hand holding Zidian.

Seeing the crack, Jin Guangyao turned back to him with exaggerated sympathy: "Ah, Jiang-zongzhu. Being your shixiong really is a thankless gig, isn't it?"

Wei Wuxian’s guard spiked; why was Jin Guangyao deliberately dragging him into the crosshairs?

Jiang Cheng fired straight back, teeth bared: "Jin-zongzhu, being your sworn brother seems a hell of a lot more dangerous!"

Jin Guangyao didn't even flinch. "You know, Jiang-zongzhu, I heard you threw quite the tantrum back at Lotus Pier yesterday. Running around like a madman with the Yiling Laozu's old sword, shoving it in front of every person you crossed, barking at them to draw it."

Jiang Cheng’s expression instantly twisted into something feral.

Wei Wuxian shot upright in Lan Wangji’s lap, his heart plummeting through his stomach.

My sword? Suibian? Didn't I leave it with Wen Ning? Wait, no—he wasn't carrying it earlier... How the hell did Jiang Cheng get his hands on it?! And why was he forcing people to unsheathe it?! Did he... did he try to draw it himself?!

As panic seized him, a pair of cool, steady hands gently stroked down his spine, Lan Wangji's quiet touch grounding him back into his body.

Noticing Jiang Cheng’s sudden, suffocating silence, Jin Guangyao’s eyes gleamed with a predatory light.

"And I hear nobody could draw that blade," Jin Guangyao crooned, "except for you. Now, isn't that peculiar? Ever since I collected that sword thirteen years ago, it has remained sealed tight. Aside from the Yiling Laozu himself, absolutely no one should be able to draw an inch of steel..."

Jiang Cheng summoned both Zidian and Sandu in a manic frenzy of crackling lightning and raw steel. "Shut your mouth!"

Jin Guangyao kept talking, smiling like a cat toying with a mouse. "Which reminded me... Back in the day, Wei-gongzi was notoriously reckless, strutting around without his spiritual sword and always cooking up the flimsiest excuses for it. I always found that terribly odd. Don't you agree?"

"What the hell are you getting at?!" Jiang Cheng roared, his voice cracking with desperation.

Jin Guangyao raised his voice, clear as a bell: "Jiang-zongzhu, you truly are remarkable. The youngest sect leader to ever rebuild Yunmeng Jiang from the ashes with his own two hands—I've always held you in deep admiration. But if memory serves, you were never quite able to beat Wei-xiansheng at anything back then. Mind telling me how you pulled off that miraculous turnaround after the Sunshot Campaign? Did you happen upon some miraculous, heavenly golden core?"

The wordsgolden coresliced through the room like a scalpel.

Jiang Cheng's face completely deformed in horror, the lightning dancing across Zidian turning dangerously erratic and blindingly white. Shaken to his very marrow, his rhythm faltered for a lethal fraction of a second.

That single opening was all Jin Guangyao had been waiting for.

A concealed chord whipped from his sleeve, whistling through the air. Jiang Cheng snapped back to reality, lashing Zidian out to intercept it. The lightning and the golden string snarled together; Jin Guangyao's palm went numb from the shock, and he dropped the chord without hesitation.

Yet he only smirked. Flicking his left wrist, a second chord whipped out from the shadows—aimed straight at Wei Wuxian!

Jiang Cheng’s pupils shrank to pinpricks. On pure, unthinking instinct, he wrenched Zidian around to intercept the lethal wire!

"Jiujiu, look out!" Jin Ling screamed.

Seizing the opening, Jin Guangyao drew the flexible soft sword coiled around his waist, driving the glittering blade straight toward Jiang Cheng's chest!

Thud.

Jiang Cheng stumbled back, clutching his chest, his face pale as death. Fresh, dark blood bubbled through his fingers, rapidly dyeing his purple robes a bruised, wet black. Across the room, having deflected the chord meant for Wei Wuxian, Zidian sputtered, flickered, and collapsed back into its dormant silver ring on Jiang Cheng's finger.

Whenever a cultivator suffered catastrophic blood loss or critical trauma, their spiritual weapons instinctively reverted to conserve their core's energy.

Jin Guangyao didn't waste a heartbeat. Stepping in close, he struck Jiang Cheng twice, sealing his spiritual meridians shut. Pulling a crisp handkerchief from his sleeve, he calmly wiped the blood from his blade, re-coiling the steel around his waist like a belt.

Jin Ling had already scrambled across the floor to catch his uncle as he collapsed.

From across the room, Lan Xichen let out a heavy sigh. "Don't jostle him. Help him sit down slowly."
